explanation: Merge two increasing streams obtained by adding 1 or √2 to earlier values. Store integer coefficient pairs so the same pair is emitted once even when reached by both streams. Advance both pointers when they propose that pair.
timeComplexity: O(k). Two-pointer versions advance each pointer at most k times; ordered-set versions pay for set operations.
spaceComplexity: O(k), including the output. The coefficient history or candidate set has at most linear size in k, as does the output.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: Every nonzero coefficient pair can be reached by adding either 1 or √2 to a smaller pair. Both candidate streams are increasing, so choosing their smaller head emits the least not-yet-emitted value. Advancing both heads when their pairs agree removes the only duplicate representation.
walkthrough: For k=3, begin with 0. The stream heads are 1 and √2, so emit 1; the new integer head is 2, so √2 follows. The answer is [0,1,√2]. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: Zero is included for every positive k.
Pairs reached from both streams must appear once.
